prose.text: "The user is in ZIA but the department rule misses them" is an attribute-mapping question. {{user-fields}} {{group-fields}}

prose.label: Which attribute is the identity.
prose.text: The user ID rules are in [[zia.ad-integration.identity-objects]], and the domain in the login must be registered as described in [[zia.scim.setup]]. {{login-from-username-only}}

prose.label: Department.
prose.text: {{enterprise-department}} {{connector-omits-department}} Whether the string must match an existing department is a separate question: [[zia.scim.groups-and-departments]].

Three points are open: which attributes are required {{gap:required-attributes}}, whether custom attributes are persisted {{gap:custom-attributes}}, and how each IdP handles department by default {{gap:per-idp-department-mapping}}.

user-fields.statement: ZIA maps these SCIM user attributes: id to a Zscaler-generated unique ID; externalId to scim_externalid; userName to the user ID (login_name) in user@domain form; displayName to the display name (user_name); groups to Groups; active to enabled or disabled; department to Department; name.givenName and name.familyName to first and last name; emails.value to scim_emails.

quotes: | id | <unique_id> | Unique ID generated by Zscaler. For example, 1a234567-1b23-1200-1234-123c |
| externalId | scim_externalid | External ID provided by the client populates onto the Zscaler user database |
The actual user ID used for authentication. The expected format is user@domain.
| displayName | User display Name (user_name) | The display name of the user |
| groups | Groups | The Groups the user belongs to |
| department | Department | The department the user belongs to |
| name.givenName | firstname | The first name of the user |
| name.familyName | lastname | The last name of the user |
When "active=false," Zscaler disables this userWhen "active=true," Zscaler enables this user
| emails.value | scim_emails | The email address of the user |

group-fields.statement: ZIA maps these SCIM group attributes: id to a Zscaler-generated unique ID, externalId to scim_externalid (kept in the Zscaler database), and displayName to the group Name.

quotes: | externalId | scim_externalid | External ID provided by the client that is kept in the Zscaler database |
| displayName | Name | Display name of the Group |

name-prefix.statement: ZIA's SCIM name attributes use the singular prefix name. (name.givenName, name.familyName); the ZPA mapping uses names.givenName.

quotes: | name.givenName | firstname | The first name of the user |
| First Name | names.givenName | The first name of the user |

enterprise-department.statement: In Zscaler's create and update examples the department is sent inside the enterprise user extension (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User), and the Go SDK models a ZIA SCIM user's department only as that extension object.

connector-omits-department.statement: A SCIM connector that sends only the core user schema, without the enterprise extension, sends no department, so the ZIA user has an empty department and department-scoped rules do not match that user.
connector-omits-department.conditions: Derived from the department being carried in the extension; whether a given connector emits the extension by default is not captured, and the consequence for rules follows from the user record lacking the value.

login-from-username-only.statement: Only the SCIM userName attribute maps to the ZIA login name; externalId and emails.value map to the reference fields scim_externalid and scim_emails.
login-from-username-only.conditions: Reads the mapping list as complete: no other attribute is mapped to login_name.

required-attributes.title: Which SCIM attributes ZIA requires
required-attributes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: The vendor doc marks only userName as required, and groups or department are needed for identity-aware policy. The captured SCIM article has no required column; Zscaler's create example sends schemas, userName, displayName and the department extension. A schema read from /Schemas on a tenant, or a vendor statement, would settle it.
required-attributes.blocks: telling an IdP admin which attributes are mandatory

custom-attributes.title: Whether ZIA persists attributes outside the documented mapping
custom-attributes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Custom SCIM attributes beyond the documented mapping are not persisted in ZIA, and the multi-valued attributes are groups and emails.value with all others single-valued. This was inferred from the ZPA article's explicit custom-attribute limitation; the ZIA article lists only the mapping above. A push of an unmapped attribute and a read-back would settle it.
custom-attributes.blocks: answering whether a custom IdP attribute can drive ZIA policy

per-idp-department-mapping.title: How each IdP maps or omits the department attribute by default
per-idp-department-mapping.detail: Entra ID, Okta and PingFederate guides are referenced by the SCIM article but their department handling is not in any captured source (former ledger zia-43). Capturing the per-IdP SAML and SCIM guides would settle it.
per-idp-department-mapping.blocks: telling operators whether their connector sends department out of the box
